textbookText: 3. Conversion of ore into suitable reducible form Calcination and Roasting Before getting metal in free and pure state some metallurgical operations are still left to be carried. The main aim of this step is to convert the metal into its suitable oxide form from which metal can be easily obtained. In case of pyrometallurgy the concentrated ore is either subjected to calcination or roasting in order to obtain metal oxide so that reduction of metal becomes easier.

Figure: calcination The process of heating concentrated ore below its melting point in a limited supply of air or in absence of air to convert ore into dry metallic oxide is called calcination. It is carried

out in case of oxide or hydroxide or carbonate ores that generally do not require oxygen to produce metal oxide. This process is carried out in a reverberatory furnace. Some examples are: When calamine is subjected to calcination it produces zinc oxide and carbon dioxide. ⎯⎯→ ZnCO3 Heat ZnO+ CO2↑ When malachite is subjected to calcination it produces copper oxide, carbon dioxide and water. ⎯⎯→ CuCO3.Cu(OH)2 Heat CuO+ CO2↑+ H2O Advantages of calcination a. The concentrated ore gets decomposed into suitable metal oxide. b. Non-metallic impurities like S, P, As, etc. get removed in the form of their volatile oxides. c. Organic matters, water of crystallization and other impurities are also removed. d. The ore becomes porous that results in easy handling. Roasting Fig: roasting of ore in blast furnace The process of heating concentrated ore below its melting point in excess supply of air to convert ore into dry metallic oxide is called roasting. It is carried out for non-oxide ore (especially for sulphide ore) to produce metal oxide. This process is also carried out in a reverberatory furnace or sinterere. Some examples are: When concentrated ore of zinc blende is subjected to roasting, then zinc oxide is produced.

⎯⎯→ 2ZnS + 3O2 Heat 2ZnO+ 2SO2↑ When concentrated ore of galena is subjected to roasting, lead oxide is produced. ⎯⎯→ 2PbS + 3O2 Heat 2PbO+ 2SO2↑ Some advantages of roasting: a. The concentrated ore gets decomposed into suitable metal oxide. b. Non-metallic impurities like S, P, As, etc. get removed in the form of their volatile oxides. c. Organic matters, water of crystallization and other impurities are also removed. d. The ore becomes porous that results in easy handling.
Test Yourself! What is the major difference between calcination and roasting?

4. Reduction Reduction is the chemical process where calcined or roasted ore is reduced with suitable reducing agents in order to get free metal. The choice of reducing agent depends upon the nature of metal and principle of metallurgy. Some common reducing agents used in metallurgy are coke(C), CO, H2, Al, Mg, Zn etc. The calcined or roasted ore consists of some kind of refractory materials (gangue) as impurities which are infusible. These impurities are removed by adding flux in the form slag. Some commonly used methods of reduction are discussed below: A. Chemical reduction methods i) Carbon reduction method (Smelting)
